question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the primary goal of palliative care?

options.A: To accelerate the process of dying
options.B: To improve the quality of life of patients and families facing life-threatening illness
options.C: To replace curative treatments completely in all hospital settings
options.D: To focus exclusively on terminal cancer patients in their final week

explanation: The primary goal defined by the WHO is to improve the quality of life for patients and their families facing life-threatening illnesses through prevention and relief of suffering. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: At what stage of a chronic, debilitating illness should palliative care ideally be integrated?

options.A: Only during the final 24 hours of life
options.B: After all curative options have completely failed for at least a year
options.C: Early in the course of the illness, alongside other therapies
options.D: Only when the patient requests discharge against medical advice

explanation: Palliative care should be integrated early in the course of illness, alongside other medical therapies aimed at prolonging life, rather than waiting until the very end. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes the palliative care stance on the dying process?

options.A: It actively seeks to accelerate death to stop suffering
options.B: It regards dying as a normal process that is neither hastened nor postponed
options.C: It attempts to reverse the dying process using advanced technology
options.D: It ignores the dying process and focuses only on physical hygiene

explanation: Palliative care affirms life and regards dying as a normal process, aiming neither to hasten nor to postpone death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does palliative care interact with life-prolonging therapies?

options.A: It must completely replace life-prolonging therapies immediately
options.B: It is only applied after all life-prolonging therapies have been stopped
options.C: It can be applied early in illness in conjunction with life-prolonging therapies
options.D: It is legally forbidden to be used alongside chemotherapy or radiation

explanation: Palliative care is applicable early in the course of illness, functioning effectively alongside other therapies intended to prolong life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of curative treatment compared to palliative care?

options.A: Eradicating the disease and restoring full health
options.C: Managing terminal pain without addressing pathology
options.D: Shortening the hospital stay for financial reasons

explanation: Curative treatment primarily focuses on eradicating the disease, reversing pathology, and restoring full health through aggressive medical or surgical interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between palliative care and curative treatment?

options.A: They are completely mutually exclusive and can never be used together
options.B: Palliative care can be provided alongside curative treatments to manage symptoms
options.C: Curative treatment is always superior and replaces palliative care entirely
options.D: Palliative care is only initiated after an autopsy is planned

explanation: Palliative care and curative treatment are not mutually exclusive and often overlap, allowing patients to receive symptom management while undergoing life-prolonging therapies. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary approach essential in palliative care?

options.A: Because doctors alone refuse to handle medication administration
options.B: Because the complex needs of seriously ill patients require diverse professional expertise
options.C: To increase the hospital bill for the patient and family
options.D: To ensure that nurses do not have to perform any clinical assessments

explanation: A multidisciplinary team is necessary because serious illness creates complex physical, emotional, and spiritual needs that span beyond the scope of a single profession. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is a common role of the nurse within the multidisciplinary palliative care team?

options.A: Acting as the primary coordinator, care provider, and communication link
options.B: Replacing the social worker in legal and financial matters entirely
options.C: Diagnosing the underlying cellular pathology of the disease
options.D: Prescribing all advanced chemotherapy regimens independently

explanation: Nurses coordinate daily care, administer medications, and serve as the primary communication link between the patient, family, and other healthcare team members. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: What does the concept of 'total pain' in palliative care refer to?

options.A: Pain that only occurs in the final stages of terminal cancer
options.B: Pain that consists of physical, emotional, social, and spiritual components
options.C: Pain that cannot be relieved by any known pharmacological agent
options.D: Physical pain caused exclusively by surgical incisions

explanation: Total pain acknowledges that suffering is complex and encompasses physical, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions that all require assessment and management. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a common nursing responsibility regarding strong opioids like morphine in palliative care?

options.A: Withholding them completely to prevent the patient from feeling drowsy
options.B: Educating patients and families to dispel fears of addiction when used for pain relief
options.C: Administering them only after the patient has lost consciousness
options.D: Ensuring the patient is monitored in an intensive care unit at all times

explanation: Nurses must educate patients and families to overcome cultural fears of addiction, explaining that proper opioid use for palliative pain management is safe and necessary. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is cultural competence essential when providing palliative care in Nigeria?

options.A: To force all patients to adopt Western death-bed practices
options.B: Because cultural and religious beliefs shape perceptions of illness, pain, and death-bed rituals
options.C: To eliminate the need for spiritual leaders in the healthcare setting
options.D: To ensure that patients do not receive any traditional medications

explanation: Nigeria's rich cultural and religious diversity influences how patients view health and dying, making cultural competence vital for respectful, personalized care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of addressing spiritual and existential needs in palliative care?

options.A: To convert the patient to a specific religion before they die
options.B: To help the patient find peace, resolve emotional distress, and address existential questions
options.C: To replace the need for physical pain management medications
options.D: To fulfill administrative hospital accreditation requirements

explanation: Addressing spiritual needs helps patients find inner peace, work through existential questions, and achieve emotional closure during serious illness. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is a common physical sign during the active dying phase that nurses should manage?

options.A: Sudden spikes in blood pressure and hyperactivity
options.B: Noisy respiratory secretions and changes in breathing patterns
options.C: Rapid muscle hypertrophy and increased appetite
options.D: Complete elimination of all bodily reflexes immediately

explanation: Signs of active dying include changes in breathing patterns and noisy respiratory secretions, which nurses manage to ensure comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h7)

question: When does bereavement support ideally begin in a comprehensive palliative care framework?

options.A: Only after the funeral ceremony has concluded
options.B: Before death through anticipatory guidance and extends into the post-death period
options.C: Only when the family requests psychiatric intervention years later
options.D: When the patient is first admitted for a minor outpatient procedure

explanation: Bereavement support begins prior to death with anticipatory guidance and continues after death to support families through their grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is a major systemic challenge Nigerian nurses often face in delivering palliative care?

options.A: An overabundance of luxury hospice facilities across rural areas
options.B: Resource limitations and restricted access to essential palliative medications like oral morphine
options.C: Complete lack of any patients requiring terminal symptom management
options.D: Mandatory laws prohibiting nurses from administering any form of pain relief

explanation: Nigerian nurses frequently encounter resource constraints and limited access to essential palliative medications such as oral morphine in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)

question: Besides direct caregiving, what is an important educational role of the nurse in palliative care in Nigeria?

options.A: Dispelling myths that associate palliative care exclusively with giving up
options.B: Convincing families to avoid all cultural and religious mourning customs
options.C: Replacing physicians in diagnosing primary disease pathology
options.D: Ensuring that patients do not receive any spiritual counseling

explanation: Nurses play an educational role by dispelling cultural myths that incorrectly view palliative care as simply 'giving up' on the patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)
